parts.title: Who Looks After The Children In Today's Britain?
parts.article:
A When Simon Baron-Cohen recently published a book, The Essential Difference, in which he claimed that the female brain is predominantly hard-wired for empathy, the male brain is predominantly hard-wired for understanding and building systems, he caught the mood of the moment. His team's experiments on day-old babies, and the finding that the male babies looked for longer at a hanging toy and the female babies longer at a face, has been repeatedly cited in the press since his book's publication. However, Elizabeth Spelke is one expert who is sceptical about whether this experiment deserves such attention. This is one isolated experiment, she says. 'Its findings fly in the face of dozens of studies on similar aspects of cognition carried out on young babies over decades. It is astonishing how much this one study has been cited, when the many studies that show no difference between the sexes, or a difference in the other direction, are ignored.'

B One of Baron-Cohen's other main studies was conducted by collecting and examining responses to questionnaires completed by adults on their own behaviour: the sort of quiz well known to readers of magazines. The answers recorded in such cases will reflect differences formed by cultural assumptions and socialisation: it is hard to see what they tell us about innate differences. Nevertheless, they have become a fashionable reference point, and recently Princess Anne, patron of Women into Science and Engineering, gave a speech in which she quoted Baron-Cohen's research as proof that six out of ten men have a systemising brain. This kind of science has passed into everyday culture, often outrunning the intentions of those who did the original work.

C Social expectations play heavily with young men and women, and expectations are in some ways more conventional in Britain today than they were ten or 20 years ago. It is particularly when they have children that women find out how society reinforces traditional expectations of their behaviour. They discover that many pressures - including the work schedule of their male partner and the expectations of his employer that it should be maintained - make it hard to combine work and home without giving their paid work a lower priority than their male colleagues do. In such a context, the claims about males' greater power to systemise and compete only serve to put further pressure on women.

D The pressures are equally powerful on men to continue in a traditional lifestyle. Some educationalists argue that among young men the concern that they might appear 'feminine' is higher than ever and may even hold back educational achievement, since studying is often seen as girlish. In later life, the drive to competitiveness in the workplace is mythologised as being tied to high levels of masculinity. Men are also told that high achievers attract more women, even though evidence shows that as women slowly become more equal at work, they begin to care less about the economic status of potential partners.

E Men are often held back from making the choice to move deeper into domestic life, and in particular childcare, feeling that it lacks status. While the gains in making a social revolution were clear for women - they could gain status and income by moving beyond the home - the gains in the parallel social revolution are harder for men to see, since it will involve them in losing status and income. The idea that men are naturally less empathetic also produces feelings of fatalism about their role. Yet there is much evidence to show that even being empathetic and good at parenting is a learned behaviour.

F It is true that, as the linguist Steven Pinker noted, in our culture women respond more readily to their children's cries, but there is nothing to say that this is down to anything other than practice and socialisation. In a culture where most men return to work straight after the birth of their children, it would be extraordinary if they did manage to remain as alert to their needs as women who remain at home. In one test carried out with teenagers, although girls said that they liked children more than boys said they did, when left alone with a crying infant, their responses were no different. Women can testify to the fact that parenting is a tricky, complicated process, not always a natural, easy role.

G However, while the definite trend of a decade ago is no longer evident, the movement towards equality has not completely stalled. A more equal sharing of childcare and even domestic labour is still desired by many men as well as women. Nearly three-quarters of young British men say that if it were financially possible they would like to stay at home to look after their families. And three-quarters of young men tell pollsters that the amount of time fathers are allowed to take off work after a birth - paternity leave - is too short in Britain. The government is therefore proposing more equal policies on maternity/paternity leave, knowing that the pressure is still forwards rather than backwards. And remember that in Britain, young men in full-time work spend about an hour a day looking after their children. That may sound paltry, but not compared to the 15 minutes they spent 30 years ago: if the time went on increasing fourfold every 30 years, equal partnership would become a reality for their grandchildren.

Questions 34–36
Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.
Write the correct letter in boxes 34–36 on your answer sheet.

Q34 What is Elizabeth Spelke’s reaction to Baron-Cohen’s experiment?

  • A She is surprised that other studies do not agree with its findings.
  • B She is confident that other research will be done in this area.
  • C She is doubtful whether it merits the notice it has been given.
  • D She is disappointed that it focused on such young infants.

Q35 According to the writer, why do mothers often put childcare above career demands?

  • A Few allowances are made for fathers to reduce their working hours.
  • B Their bosses are not keen to employ them for full-time work.
  • C They find that the competitive workplace loses its attraction.
  • D The social benefit system encourages them to stay at home.

Q36 What does the writer suggest about women as parents in paragraph F?

  • A They are naturally well suited to looking after children.
  • B They have to work at mastering the skills of motherhood.
  • C Their hearing is naturally attuned so they can respond to babies.
  • D Their natural desire is to stay at home to care for children.
Questions 37–40
Complete the summary below.
Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.
Write your answers in boxes 37–40 on your answer sheet.
Men and childcare
One reason why some men may be unwilling to leave their jobs to look after their children is because the gains that could come with such a change are not obvious. Staying at home would in fact mean accepting a considerable drop in pay and in . The conventional notion that men are not as as women may also lead men to experience a certain sense of resignation about their traditional place in society. However, it is interesting to note that the majority of young men in the UK say that the statutory time permitted for is inadequate. Influence is thus being exerted on the to review the existing provision.

reference:
Q27

解析 D段明确指出，教育学家认为年轻男性担心显得“女性化”，这阻碍了他们的学业表现。

干扰 你可能会因为没认出“educational achievement”是题干“academic performance（学业表现）”的同义替换而漏掉这段。

句子 Some educationalists argue that among young men the concern that they might appear 'feminine' is higher than ever and may even hold back educational achievement, since studying is often seen as girlish.

Q28

解析 F段对比了社会文化下女性对孩子哭声的快速反应，以及男性因为早早返回工作岗位而无法像女性那样对孩子的需求保持警觉。

干扰 你可能会在A段看到关于婴儿的研究就误选，但A段对比的是男女婴儿，而F段才是对比父母对婴儿需求的反应。

句子 It is true that, as the linguist Steven Pinker noted, in our culture women respond more readily to their children's cries, but there is nothing to say that this is down to anything other than practice and socialisation. In a culture where most men return to work straight after the birth of their children, it would be extraordinary if they did manage to remain as alert to their needs as women who remain at home.

Q29

解析 D段末尾提到，随着女性在工作中地位更加平等，她们开始较少关注潜在伴侣的经济地位。

干扰 你可能会被前文关于男性竞争力的描述干扰，其实答案直接对应段落最后一句话中“care less about the economic status”这一转变。

句子 Men are also told that high achievers attract more women, even though evidence shows that as women slowly become more equal at work, they begin to care less about the economic status of potential partners.

Q30

解析 A段开头介绍了一项针对刚出生一天大的婴儿进行的实验及其发现。

干扰 你可能看到“study”就去盲目寻找实验数据，但A段的“experiments on day-old babies”直接且唯一地匹配了关于婴儿行为的研究。

句子 His team's experiments on day-old babies, and the finding that the male babies looked for longer at a hanging toy and the female babies longer at a face, has been repeatedly cited in the press since his book's publication.

Q31

解析 G段最后预测，如果男性照顾孩子的时间按现在的速度增长，孙子辈就能实现真正的男女平等分担。

干扰 你可能会被前面的政策提议吸引注意力，但真正的“prediction（预测）”出现在段落最后一句的虚拟语气中。

句子 That may sound paltry, but not compared to the 15 minutes they spent 30 years ago: if the time went on increasing fourfold every 30 years, equal partnership would become a reality for their grandchildren.

Q32

解析 B段提到了一项通过收集成人填写的问卷来分析行为的研究，这种问卷就是杂志读者很熟悉的自测题。

干扰 你可能会对“self-assessment method（自我评估法）”感到陌生，它在原文中被直白地替换成了“questionnaires completed by adults on their own behaviour”以及“quiz”。

句子 One of Baron-Cohen's other main studies was conducted by collecting and examining responses to questionnaires completed by adults on their own behaviour: the sort of quiz well known to readers of magazines.

Q33

解析 F段提到了一项针对青少年（teenagers）进行的测试，观察他们与哭泣的婴儿独处时的反应。

干扰 你可能会把注意力放在A段的婴儿实验上，但本题问的是“adolescents（青少年）”的反应，也就是F段的“teenagers”。

句子 In one test carried out with teenagers, although girls said that they liked children more than boys said they did, when left alone with a crying infant, their responses were no different.

Q34

解析 Elizabeth Spelke表示怀疑这个实验是否配得上它所受到的关注，并指出这只是一个孤立的实验。

干扰 你可能想选择A，但原文并不是说她对“其他研究不同意”感到惊讶，而是对“这一个孤立研究被过度引用”感到震惊和怀疑。

句子 However, Elizabeth Spelke is one expert who is sceptical about whether this experiment deserves such attention. This is one isolated experiment, she says. 'Its findings fly in the face of dozens of studies on similar aspects of cognition carried out on young babies over decades. It is astonishing how much this one study has been cited, when the many studies that show no difference between the sexes, or a difference in the other direction, are ignored.

Q35

解析 女性发现男方伴侣的工作时间安排和老板的期望导致男方无法兼顾家庭，这就迫使女性不得不降低自己工作的优先级。

干扰 你可能想选择B或C，但原文强调的核心压力来源于男方雇主对男性保持传统工作时长的期望（没有给父亲减少工作时间的余地）。

句子 It is particularly when they have children that women find out how society reinforces traditional expectations of their behaviour. They discover that many pressures - including the work schedule of their male partner and the expectations of his employer that it should be maintained - make it hard to combine work and home without giving their paid work a lower priority than their male colleagues do.

Q36

解析 作者在F段借女性之口证明，做父母是一个需要面对复杂技巧的过程，而并非天生就容易的本能。

干扰 你可能想选择A（天生适合），但这完全违背了原文最后一句“不是一个天生容易的角色”的核心思想。

句子 Women can testify to the fact that parenting is a tricky, complicated process, not always a natural, easy role.

Q37

解析 原文明确提到男性回归家庭意味着他们将失去“status and income（地位和收入）”，对应题干的“drop in pay and in...”。

干扰 你可能会填“income”，但题干前面已经给出了“drop in pay”，因此只能填并列的“status”。

句子 While the gains in making a social revolution were clear for women - they could gain status and income by moving beyond the home - the gains in the parallel social revolution are harder for men to see, since it will involve them in losing status and income.

Q38

解析 原文指出认为男性天生不如女性“empathetic（有同理心）”的观点，会让男性对自己的角色产生宿命感。

干扰 你可能会顺着前文找竞争力相关的词，但这里直接考察“are naturally less empathetic”的照搬，题干是“not as ___ as women”。

句子 The idea that men are naturally less empathetic also produces feelings of fatalism about their role.

Q39

解析 原文提到四分之三的年轻男性告诉民意调查员，英国父亲在孩子出生后获准休假的“paternity leave（陪产假）”时间太短了。

干扰 你可能会填“time”或“off work”，但破折号中间的专有名词“paternity leave”才是准确指代“statutory time permitted”的核心答案。

句子 And three-quarters of young men tell pollsters that the amount of time fathers are allowed to take off work after a birth - paternity leave - is too short in Britain.

Q40

解析 原文指出，由于压力仍在向前推动，所以“government（政府）”正在提议制定更平等的产假/陪产假政策（即重新审查现有规定）。

干扰 你可能会在原文中迷失施动者，但这里的句子主语“The government”正是受到影响并提议新政的主体。

句子 The government is therefore proposing more equal policies on maternity/paternity leave, knowing that the pressure is still forwards rather than backwards.
